description: Protective detection indicators for the browser agent security layer. These indicators identify states where the agent should warn, pause, block, or request human oversight. They are not bypass instructions.

decision_hints.warn: Continue only if the caller or policy allows risk-tolerant execution.
decision_hints.block: Stop automated action and require explicit human review or an alternate safe path.

low.description: Minor risk or weak signal; usually warn only when combined.

medium.description: Meaningful risk or protected interaction; usually warn.

high.description: Strong protective signal; often block depending on policy.

critical.description: Sensitive or unsafe state; block by default.

captcha.description: Human-verification and CAPTCHA challenges. The agent should stop or request human oversight rather than trying to bypass the challenge.

text: checking if the site connection is secure
confirm you are not a robot
review the security of your connection

false_positive_hints: A page that only mentions 'captcha' in a blog post, FAQ, or documentation body is not itself a challenge; require a matching selector/URL or an active challenge widget.
Some sites embed a captcha widget on every page load (e.g. comment forms) without it being an active blocking challenge; check widget visibility/state, not just presence in the DOM.
notes: Detection is protective only; do not automate challenge solving or evasion.

bot_detection_block.description: Bot-detection, anti-automation, WAF, and automated-access blocks.

text: not allowed to access this page
this request has been identified as automated

false_positive_hints: Generic 403/'forbidden' text can also come from misconfigured routes, expired links, or normal auth failures unrelated to bot detection; corroborate with a vendor-specific selector, header, or cookie before treating as bot detection.

Server headers like 'cloudflare' are extremely common (most sites sit behind Cloudflare CDN) and are not themselves a block signal; only weight them when combined with a challenge cookie or block-page text.
notes: Treat as a site-protection signal, not as a prompt to evade controls.

rate_limit.description: Rate-limiting and quota exhaustion signals. The agent should back off and avoid repeated requests.
false_positive_hints: A one-off 503 during a deploy or a transient network blip is not sustained rate limiting; treat isolated occurrences as low-confidence and re-check after a short backoff.
Some apps show 'please try again later' for unrelated validation errors; corroborate with a 429 status or rate-limit headers when possible.
notes: Use configured backoff rather than repeated immediate retries.

login_auth_wall.description: Login, authentication, SSO, MFA, session-expiry, or account-wall states.
false_positive_hints: A visible 'sign in' link in a site's global navigation is normal and not itself a wall; only treat as a wall when it blocks the requested content/action.
Marketing pages that mention 'create an account' as a call-to-action (not a gate) should not trigger this on their own.
notes: Warn because credentials or user-specific authorization may be required.

permission_access_denied.description: Permission-denied and authorization failure states that may indicate private or restricted content.
false_positive_hints: A 403 on a single sub-resource (e.g. an analytics beacon) while the main page loads fine is not the same as the page itself being restricted.
Some sites return 401/403 briefly during session refresh; treat single transient occurrences as low-confidence.
notes: Do not attempt to bypass access controls; surface the state to the caller.

unsafe_url_scheme.description: URL schemes that should not be navigated by an automated browser agent unless explicitly allowed by policy.
false_positive_hints: 'data:' URIs used only for inline images/fonts within otherwise normal navigation are lower risk than a top-level navigation to a data: URI; weight navigation target higher than embedded resource usage.
'view-source:' or 'about:' pages the user explicitly opened themselves (not agent-initiated navigation) may be expected in some debugging workflows; confirm navigation origin.
notes: http and https are the default allowed navigation schemes.

private_network_or_local_target.description: Localhost, private-network, loopback, link-local, and cloud-metadata targets that can expose internal services or credentials.
false_positive_hints: Legitimate developer/test workflows may intentionally target localhost or a private IP; if the task explicitly requests local/dev testing under an approved policy, this may be an expected allowlisted exception rather than a true positive.
A string like '127.0.0.1' appearing only in page text/documentation (not as a navigation or request target) is informational, not a navigation risk.
notes: Protects against SSRF-style browsing and accidental access to local/internal services.

dangerous_download_or_execution.description: Executable, script, installer, or package downloads that may execute code or alter the host system.
false_positive_hints: Legitimate software vendor download pages (official installers from a known, verified domain) are expected in some workflows; combine with domain reputation/allowlists before blocking outright.
A file extension like '.js' appearing as a static asset reference (e.g. a script tag) is not the same as an offered download; scope this matcher to download/attachment contexts.
notes: Warn or block depending on product policy; do not execute downloaded content automatically.

credential_or_secret_exposure.description: Credentials, API keys, access tokens, private keys, session cookies, and other secrets in page content, URLs, forms, or action payloads.
false_positive_hints: Placeholder or example values in documentation (e.g. 'sk-xxxxxxxx', 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE') are not real secrets; require a plausible entropy/format match, not just the surrounding label text.

Autofill password fields on a login form the user is legitimately signing into are expected UI, not exposure; this matcher is about secrets appearing in visible text/URLs/logs, not normal password input fields.
notes: Evidence should be redacted by default. Prefer detection metadata over raw secret values.

payment_financial_data.description: Payment-card, bank-account, tax, or financial identifiers that should not be logged or replayed.
false_positive_hints: Generic references to 'billing address' or 'tax id' in a privacy policy or terms page are informational text, not actual data entry/exposure.
A masked card number display (e.g. '**** **** **** 1234') is lower risk than a fully exposed PAN; weight partial/masked matches lower than full-number regex hits.
notes: Do not store raw financial identifiers in memory, logs, or test fixtures.

personal_data_pii.description: Personal data and identity information that may require privacy-preserving handling.
false_positive_hints: Generic form labels like 'email address' or 'phone number' on an ordinary signup form are expected UI text, not an exposure event; this is most useful when actual values (not just field labels) are matched.
Public business contact information (e.g. a company's published support email) is not sensitive personal data in the same way a user's own PII is.
notes: PII detection can be noisy; treat as warning unless policy requires blocking.

phishing_social_engineering.description: Phishing, credential-harvesting, social-engineering, or coercive payment signals.
false_positive_hints: Legitimate account-security emails/pages from known providers may use similar urgency language ('unusual sign-in attempt', 'verify your account'); corroborate with sender/domain reputation before treating as phishing.

Customer support tools that legitimately need remote-access software (TeamViewer, AnyDesk) in an enterprise IT context are a normal use case; context (unsolicited pop-up vs. requested support session) matters.
notes: Warn the caller; avoid entering credentials or payment data into suspicious flows.

crypto_wallet_sensitive_flow.description: Cryptocurrency wallet, seed phrase, private key, or irreversible transaction prompts.
false_positive_hints: A news article or educational page that discusses seed phrases or wallet security conceptually (without an active connect/sign prompt) should not trigger a block.
A user knowingly using a legitimate, expected DeFi/exchange workflow under explicit human direction may be a policy-approved exception rather than a true positive.
notes: Block automated entry or signing actions. Human review required.

insecure_form_or_transport.description: Forms, credential fields, or sensitive inputs over insecure or mixed-content transport.
false_positive_hints: Some internal/dev/staging environments intentionally use self-signed certificates or http; this may be an expected exception under an approved policy rather than a genuine risk.
A page merely mentioning 'SSL' or 'TLS' in help documentation is not itself an insecure-transport event.
notes: Combine with current page scheme and form action before blocking.

destructive_or_irreversible_action.description: Browser-visible prompts that indicate deletion, payment, submission, publishing, or irreversible account changes.
false_positive_hints: Buttons like 'submit' or 'place order' are extremely common UI text; only elevate confidence when combined with a clearly destructive/financial context (e.g. near a total, a delete confirmation dialog, or an account-closure flow).
A disabled or greyed-out destructive button is not an actionable state.
notes: This is a protective confirmation signal; downstream policy decides whether to pause.

file_upload_sensitive.description: File-upload controls and prompts that may expose local files or sensitive documents.
false_positive_hints: A generic 'upload file' control for non-sensitive content (e.g. a profile picture) is lower risk than an explicit request for an ID, passport, or financial document; weight by the specific document type requested.
File-upload UI present on the page but not actively being engaged by the agent is informational, not an action in progress.
notes: Avoid automatic local file selection unless explicitly requested and policy-approved.

cookie_consent_or_privacy_banner.description: Cookie consent, privacy choices, and tracking-preference banners. Usually not unsafe, but useful for automation decisions and user privacy.
false_positive_hints: This category is intentionally low-risk/informational; it should rarely if ever block a workflow on its own.
notes: Privacy banner detection is informational unless the product policy requires a specific choice.

adult_or_sensitive_content_boundary.description: Age-gated, adult, gambling, weapons, drugs, or other sensitive content boundaries that may require policy checks.
false_positive_hints: Words like 'casino' or 'firearms' appearing in unrelated news coverage, historical content, or regulatory text are not the same as an active age-gated or transactional page; weight page context (age-gate UI, purchase flow) over a single keyword hit.
Review/rating sites, news articles, and educational content about these topics are lower risk than a direct storefront or gambling transaction page.
notes: Signal for product policy evaluation; do not infer illegality from a single weak match.

browser_or_extension_permission_prompt.description: Browser, OS, or extension permission prompts that may expose device capabilities or user data.
false_positive_hints: A page merely explaining why it might ask for a permission (help text) is not the same as an active native permission prompt.
Permission requests the human user directly and intentionally triggered themselves (not the agent) may be expected in some assisted workflows.
notes: Automation should not grant sensitive device permissions by default.

malicious_script_or_xss_signal.description: Visible or URL-level signals of script injection, XSS payloads, or suspicious encoded script execution.
false_positive_hints: Normal, legitimate JavaScript on nearly every modern site uses 'localStorage', 'sessionStorage', 'eval(' (rarely but sometimes), or event handler attributes; this matcher is best scoped to reflected/URL-borne payloads or injection contexts rather than ordinary inline site JavaScript.
Security research, documentation, or educational pages that display example XSS payloads as inert text are not themselves an active injection attempt.
notes: Primarily protective for navigation/action payloads and reflected content diagnostics.

legal_or_compliance_wall.description: Legal, terms, compliance, export-control, or consent gates that may require human acknowledgement.
false_positive_hints: A simple footer link to a 'privacy policy' or 'terms of service' page, present on virtually every site, is not itself a wall; only elevate when it actively blocks progress (e.g. a modal requiring 'I agree' before continuing).
notes: Usually a warning; product policy determines whether automated acknowledgement is allowed.

geo_or_region_block.description: Geographic or region-based access restrictions, including region-locked content and VPN/proxy detection notices.

text: content is not available in your country
content not available in your region
not licensed to stream in your country
service is unavailable in your area
this content is not available in your location

false_positive_hints: Some sites show a soft regional preference banner (e.g. 'switch to your local store') without actually blocking access; only elevate when content or navigation is actually prevented.
notes: Informational for most workflows; do not attempt to spoof location or use VPNs/proxies to bypass regional restrictions.

maintenance_or_outage_page.description: Planned maintenance, scheduled downtime, or service-outage pages indicating the site is temporarily unavailable for reasons unrelated to rate limiting or blocking.
false_positive_hints: A single slow-loading request is not the same as a maintenance page; require matching page text/selectors rather than status code alone, since 503 overlaps with rate_limit and bot_detection_block.
notes: Distinct from rate_limit: this indicates planned/expected downtime rather than a signal to back off request volume. Retry later rather than repeatedly polling.

oauth_third_party_consent_grant.description: Third-party OAuth/consent screens requesting the user grant an application access to account data or scopes. Distinct from a plain login wall because it involves authorizing a specific app's permissions.

text: grant access to your Google Account
has requested permission to access your account

false_positive_hints: A user's own first-party login to a site they already use is not the same as a third-party app requesting a scope grant; require an explicit 'authorize'/'grant access' consent UI, not just any OAuth-flavored URL.
notes: Review requested scopes carefully before approving; do not grant broad or unnecessary permissions on the user's behalf without explicit human confirmation.

fake_system_alert_or_tech_support_scam.description: Fake virus/security alerts, fraudulent tech-support pop-ups, and scareware pages designed to pressure the user into calling a number, downloading software, or granting remote access.

text: do not turn off your computer
your device is infected with a virus
your ip address has been flagged

false_positive_hints: Legitimate OS/browser security warnings (e.g. a real browser's own malware-download interstitial) use standard browser chrome, not in-page content; verify whether the alert is native browser UI versus page-rendered content mimicking one.
notes: These pages are designed to induce panic; never call listed numbers, download 'fixes', or grant remote access. Always block and surface for human review.

unexpected_domain_redirect_or_typosquat.description: Navigation that lands on a domain different from the one requested/expected, including punycode/IDN homograph patterns and common typosquatting indicators.
false_positive_hints: Many legitimate flows redirect across domains on purpose (payment processors, SSO providers, CDN-hosted assets, link shorteners); this is most useful when combined with a known expected-destination allowlist rather than flagging every cross-domain redirect.
notes: Best used by comparing the final navigation target against the originally requested/linked domain rather than in isolation (domain_compare: flag when the final landing domain differs from the originally requested/linked domain and is not a known, expected redirect such as shortener-to-destination).

ad_or_popup_interstitial.description: Advertising interstitials, pop-ups, pop-unders, and 'you have won' style promotional overlays that interrupt the primary task.

text: click here to claim your prize

false_positive_hints: Ordinary, non-deceptive display advertising (e.g. a banner ad) is lower risk than a prize/reward-claim overlay; this matcher is aimed at deceptive/scammy interstitials rather than routine ad content.
notes: Usually safe to dismiss/close rather than block outright, but avoid clicking through prize-claim style overlays.
